plan.name: Keep repository checks off modeled projects
plan.summary: Reserve a repository's modeled projects directory for the gate through an optional projects_directory field in its committed repository contract, using invariant when omitted and allowing a different clean repository-relative directory; preserve the serialized identity of contracts that omit the field. Add init -projects with that same default, draft the directory without treating its projects as application parts, and print specific TypeScript exclude and ESLint ignore guidance for each enclosing TypeScript part, including when keeping an existing contract, while explaining why drivers keep their .ts imports and leaving application configuration untouched. Run configured checks and native acceptance on private copies with only the captured projects directory removed, on both base and candidate paths and through check-repository, while retaining the complete original checkout for scope, ratification and the gate's project toolchains and preserving command arguments, application files, dependency verification, failures and cleanup. Refuse unsafe or conflicting directory declarations, application parts or dependency inputs inside that directory, and configured native acceptance or implicit regression tests placed there, so candidate configuration cannot hide application checks. Update SPEC.md and the linked docs/factory.md page with the directory contract, init guidance, migration for custom watch -projects paths and check isolation, citing [#779's ratified plan](.invariant/plans/issue-779.json) as this decision's record.

tests.name: TestInitExplainsProjectExclusions779
tests.says: Init explains TypeScript and ESLint exclusions before projects exist and when preserving an existing contract, without editing application configuration.

tests.name: TestInitProjectsFlag779
tests.says: Init drafts a custom projects directory, excludes it from application parts, respects that declaration on reruns, prints matching watch and exclusion guidance, and rejects unsafe paths before writing.

tests.name: TestDraftSeparatesModeledProjects779
tests.says: Repository drafts reserve invariant for modeled projects, keep similarly named application parts, agree for disk and held evidence, and leave all source bytes intact.

tests.name: TestProjectsDirectoryIsCapturedAndValidated779
tests.says: The committed contract captures a safe projects directory, preserves omitted-field serialization, and rejects unsafe paths, links, file destinations and conflicts with application parts or dependencies.

tests.name: TestConfiguredCommandsExcludeProjects779
tests.says: All four configured commands in Go, Python and TypeScript see application files but no modeled-project tree; exact arguments, application failures, driver imports and cleanup are preserved.

tests.name: TestConfiguredCustomProjectsUseCapturedAuthority779
tests.says: A custom nested projects directory comes only from captured base policy; candidate policy cannot conceal application code, similarly named paths remain visible, and staging still refuses links.

tests.name: TestNativeChecksExcludeProjectsOnBaseAndCandidate779
tests.says: Independent native base failures and candidate passes use fresh project-free environments while preserving full original trees, pinned test identities and cleanup.

tests.name: TestProjectDirectoryCannotHideAcceptanceOrRegressions779
tests.says: Go, pytest, Vitest and Jest cannot place native acceptance or implicitly admitted regressions inside the excluded projects directory; neighboring application tests remain eligible.

tests.name: TestRepositoryCILeavesProjectsToGate779
tests.says: Push, ordinary PR and modeled factory PR repository checks exclude projects while still running every application phase, preserving drivers for modeled verification and keeping scope and ratification behavior.
